PLANTING_PLAN.status: Recommended cultivars for every open spot in R1 to R12; nothing is bought or grafted yet
PLANTING_PLAN.summary: Chosen in October 2026 for a short-season U-pick orchard at about 4,750 ft with roughly 70 to 110 frost-free days. Disease-resistant apples that ripen early or in mid-season fill R4 to R6 and the grafted row R1; hardy tart and sweet cherries, European plums, a Seckel pear, and replacements for the dead pear, cherry and peach fill the rest. R13 to R15 stay open for later.
PLANTING_PLAN.rootstock_advice: Ask nurseries for semi-dwarf trees (about 60 to 75 percent of standard; G.890, G.214 or M.7 for apples). The grid is 18 x 20 ft and the site is dry and windy, so dwarf stocks (M.27, M.9, B.9) would need permanent stakes and leave gaps.
PLANTING_PLAN.graft_advice: The 13 grafts in R1 go onto rootstocks you already own: 11 M-111 (vigorous, semi-standard), 2 EMLA 7 (semi-dwarf) and 1 of unknown type, so one rootstock is left as a spare. Order scionwood in winter from a nursery that sells it for spring 2027 (some sell out early), keep it cold and damp until grafting, and graft in early spring as the rootstock buds begin to swell. Use the two EMLA 7 rootstocks for Redfree, a vigorous scion (its third tree goes on an M-111), and put lower-vigor scions such as Pixie Crunch on the vigorous M-111. Grafted trees take longer to bear than bought trees. Check that a cultivar may be propagated at home before ordering scionwood.
PLANTING_PLAN.shipping_note: Confirm that each nursery ships the item to Idaho before ordering; some retailers exclude Idaho for some items.

items.rootstock: Semi-dwarf wanted; G.214 is cold-hardy and fire-blight resistant
items.role: Early block: the first apples of the season
items.caution: Ripens unevenly over about a week, so plan on more than one picking; keeps about six weeks in the fridge. Sources put its bloom early, in group 1 to 2, so group 2 is a planning value.

items.rootstock: Semi-dwarf wanted; G.890 (about 60 percent of standard) is offered
items.role: Early-to-mid September apple; hardy to about -50 F
items.caution: Medium fruit with a mild flavor and a licorice note; bears heavily, so thin the crop.

items.rootstock: Semi-dwarf wanted; nurseries list EMLA 27 or M.26 dwarfs, too small for 18 x 20 ft spacing
items.role: Large crisp sweet-tart apple for mid to late September
items.caution: Cummins lists bloom group 3 and diploid. Raintree puts harvest in late September but Cummins calls it early-ripening, so its timing here is uncertain.

items.rootstock: Size-controlling semi-dwarf wanted; nurseries often ship it on MM.111, which stays large
items.role: Large striped-red apple for early October; very disease resistant
items.caution: Ripens with Delicious (about Oct 5 at Geneva, NY), so it is a gamble in a short season. Vigorous, spreading tree. No source gave its flowering group, so group 3 is assumed.

items.rootstock: M.7 semi-dwarf; B.9 dwarf is also offered but too small here
items.role: October pie and cider apple; zone 3, late bloom
items.caution: Bloom group 4 comes from a single nursery page (Roots to Fruits). Ripens in mid-October, the latest of the new apples, and is tart rather than a fresh-eating favorite.

items.rootstock: Semi-dwarf wanted; nurseries list M.27 or EMLA 26 dwarfs, too small here
items.role: One-tree test of a very early yellow apple
items.caution: Sources disagree on ripening (mid-July or August) and zone (4 to 9 or 5 to 8), and Purdue rates it susceptible to cedar-apple rust, with junipers on site. No source gave its flowering group, so group 2 is assumed.

items.rootstock: OHxF 87 (semi-dwarf, cold-hardy, fire-blight resistant)
items.role: Fire-blight-resistant European pear that ripens early
items.caution: Not self-fertile. Only one pollination partner counts within 50 ft (Red Bartlett at 49 ft), so fruit set may be light. A fifth Asian pear would have Hosui and Hardy Giant beside it.

items.rootstock: Mazzard or another canker-tolerant stock; avoid Gisela 6, the most canker-susceptible (Intermountain Fruit)
items.role: Hardy, late-blooming, canker-resistant dark sweet cherry
items.caution: Blooms later than Bing, so it adds no pollen for the Bing or Black Tartarian trees, which still depend on Lapins at R10-C2. Birds need netting.

items.rootstock: Krymsk 86 was suggested (cold-hardy, anchors well, near-standard size); canker tolerance of the rootstock is unverified
items.role: Bud-hardy, self-fertile mid-season freestone
items.caution: Peaches here carry bacterial canker (untreated positives). Prune only in dry weather, use dormant copper, and buy clean certified stock.

items.rootstock: Your EMLA 7 rootstocks (it is a vigorous scion), then M-111
items.role: Earliest graft: ripe toward the end of August, with a very good cedar-apple rust rating (Purdue)
items.caution: Ripens over several weeks, so plan on picking in stages, and keeps only 1 to 3 months. Scionwood showed sold out at Cummins in mid-October while another nursery had stock, so order early.

items.rootstock: Your M-111 rootstock

items.caution: The orchard already has three crabapples (Kerr, Dolgo, Wickson); this one is larger, about 2 inches, with a nutty flavor mild enough for fresh eating. Cummins says it blooms early over a long period, so a spring frost can cost a crop.
